visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the binary-search midpoint at index 5, eliminates the left half, and keeps the active range [6,10], while Lesson 2 contradicts its own formula mid=floor((7+7)/2)=7 by leaving low and high visually at indices 0 and 10 instead of both at 7.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a concrete, wired quiz gate after act_found with a real question, answer options, and a marked correct answer, while Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan JSON and therefore no evidence of any functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has consistently clear, natural, well-paced narration with math spoken appropriately as 'O of log n,' while Lesson 1 is mostly understandable but ends with a defective dangling fragment ('Given the sorted array, 3...') and feels less polished.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides mostly synchronized visual cues at the moments the narration introduces pointers, midpoints, comparisons, and results, whereas Lesson 1 has no beat/timing cue data at all despite referencing many visual search steps, making its sync unverifiable and effectively absent.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 provides a clearer pedagogical build with low/high/mid pointers, repeated halving, and a stronger O(log n) explanation, while Lesson 1 is more superficial and even has an odd trailing fragment, though Lesson 2 is not perfect because its plan incorrectly says linear search would take 7 steps and the script under-explains the 56 comparison.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a cleaner, more consistent dark theme with legible centered title text and a coherent visualization, while Lesson 1 is cluttered by browser/app chrome, chat widgets/tooltips, excessive empty space, and mid-lesson content pushed awkwardly into the lower right.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner, taking five of six dimensions with generally high confidence: interactivity (0.99), narration quality (0.93), sync (0.95), concept accuracy (0.74), and polish (0.92). These wins indicate it is more complete, better paced, more interactive, and more professionally presented. Lesson 1 strongly wins visual accuracy (0.93) because Lesson 2 contains a notable pointer/midpoint inconsistency, so Lesson 2 is not flawless. However, the majority of high-confidence judgments favor Lesson 2, and the split is not close enough to justify a tie.
